title: Activation Sprint — First Quarter Customer Activation Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, runnable sprint plan for the first 90 days after contract signature (aka the Activation Sprint). It is designed to be used by the CSM + Solutions Engineering pair to drive predictable time-to-value, capture early renewal signals, and create a handoff bundle for renewal planning.

Audience:
CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Implementation PMs, Customer Success Managers, Customer Admins.

Quick orientation (how to use):
- Copy this doc into the customer folder and replace bracketed placeholders.
- Run daily standups during Week 0–2. Move to weekly cadence after day 21 unless risk flagged.
- Track the "Risk Score" and the "Value Milestones" in the renewal tracker table below.

Activation sprint summary (at-a-glance):
- Day 0: Kickoff + access verified + success criteria agreed.
- Days 1–14: Core integration, first proof-of-value (POV) workflow, training for 2 named users.
- Days 15–30: Embed usage patterns, first 2 production requests, baseline metrics.
- Days 31–60: Expansion of use cases, performance tuning, rollout to broader user group.
- Days 61–90: Stabilization, QBR prep, renewal readiness scorecard.

Roles & responsibilities (recommended):
- CSM (owner): drive cadence, stakeholders, adoption plan, renewal risk.
- Solutions Engineer: integration support, runbooks, troubleshooting, first-query success.
- Implementation PM: project plan, timelines, blocker removal.
- Customer Technical Lead: provide access, data mappings, review runbook.

Minimum success criteria (sign-off items):
- 2 production-grade requests processed end-to-end (latency within SLA or noted).
- Customer-defined value metric improved from baseline (or clear baseline recorded).
- Admin users trained and knowledge transfer session recorded.
- Health dashboard created and shared with customer execs.

Daily/Weekly rituals (sample cadence):
- Day 0 (Kickoff meeting agenda): Introductions, goals, critical success metrics, access checklist, timeline, risks, next steps (15–30m).
- Daily (Weeks 0–2): 15m standup: blocked items, next 24h plan, immediate wins.
- Weekly (Weeks 3–12): 30m status review: adoption metrics, outstanding issues, plan for next week, decisions needed.
- Biweekly executive email (from CSM): short status + one ask.

Concrete checklists (copy and paste into customer folder):
- Day 0 access checklist: API keys issued, firewall rules, test dataset uploaded, admin accounts created, SSO info collected.
- SE runbook checklist: sample prompt tests, KV cache warm-up plan, baseline latency measurement, quantization profile selection notes.
- Training checklist: slide deck reviewed, recording scheduled, 2 power users assigned, knowledge base article links added.

Risk scoring (simple 0–10, track in tracker):
- 0–2: Green (on track)
- 3–5: Yellow (requires minor intervention)
- 6–8: Orange (escalation to manager + SE)
- 9–10: Red (exec escalation + stop-gap fallback)
Drivers (examples): access delays, inaccurate data mapping, performance regressions, missing decision-maker, scope creep.

Renewal signals to capture (automated if possible):
- Usage engagement (DAU/WAU for core users)
- Value metric trajectory (e.g., queries/converted workflows, cost-per-request improvements)
- Billing anomalies or unexpected consumption spikes
- Support ticket velocity and severity (tickets/week and P1s)
- Exec engagement (meetings with budget owner > twice)

Renewal outreach triggers (sample policy):
- 30 days before renewal: Identify renewal owner and create renewal plan draft.
- 60 days before renewal: Present consumption vs committed and adoption plan.
- <30 days and risk score >=6: Launch renewal rescue play (discount + targeted implementation scope).

30 / 60 / 90 decomposed checklist (practical items):
- 0–30 (Foundation):
  - Confirm success criteria, baseline metrics, initial admin + API access, run first production request, record training.
  - Deliverable: "Go-live checklist" + recording.
- 31–60 (Scale):
  - Expand to additional user groups, set up monitoring dashboards, implement recommended batching/cache settings, tune model variant if latency issues.
  - Deliverable: "Adoption dashboard" + example of baseline vs current metric.
- 61–90 (Optimize & Renew):
  - Work on performance/cost tradeoffs (quantization recommendation), capture case studies, schedule QBR (30–45m) with execs.
  - Deliverable: "90-day health pack" and renewal readiness score (Green/Yellow/Red).

Sample QBR agenda (30–45 minutes):
- 5m: Exec recap and stated objectives
- 10m: Usage & value metrics (baseline -> current)
- 10m: Roadmap alignment + next 90 days (operational asks)
- 5m: Risks & mitigation plan
- 5m: Renewal/next steps and ask (clear call to action)

Simple renewal tracker (plain text table for quick copy):
Customer | Contract start | Renewal date | Renewal owner | Risk score | Value metric | Last exec touch
Acme Corp | 2024-10-01 | 2025-10-01 | Ava Martinez | 3 | 12% latency improvement | 2024-11-01
Beta Inc | 2024-09-15 | 2025-09-15 | Jun Park | 6 | Onboarding in progress | 2024-10-20

Sample email templates (short & low friction):
- Day 0 welcome (CSM):
Subject: Welcome + Day 0 checklist 
Hi [Name],
Thanks for choosing Redwood Inference. Quick agenda for today: confirm access, success metric, and timeline. Please share [list items]. We’ll run the first test at [time].

- 2-week check-in (CSM):
Subject: 2-week check-in — quick sync?
Hi [Name],
We’re seeing early progress: first workflows live. 10–15m to align on blockers and next expansions?

- 30-day value summary (CSM):
Subject: 30-day summary + next steps
Hi [Name],
Attached: 30-day snapshot (usage, performance, issues). Recommended next steps: expand to X team, enable caching, schedule QBR.

- Rescue outreach (if risk >=6):
Subject: Focused plan to hit SLA and adoption targets
Hi [Name],
We’ve identified the top 3 blockers and a focused 2-week plan to address them. Can we lock 3 hours of SE time and 1 executive touch to accelerate?

Operational notes / TODOs (in-doc):
- [ ] Make copy of this template into customer folder and replace placeholders.
- [ ] Add data export link from instrumentation (tracking id CUST-1123).
- [ ] Create dashboard in Looker/Metabase with the 3 value metrics.
- [ ] Add escalation path contact info (on-call SE + manager).

Low fidelity metrics to track (start simple):
- API calls per day (top 10 users)
- Mean latency per model variant
- Success rate (end-to-end)
- Tickets/week and P1s
- Exec touchpoints per 30 days

Notes from recent pilots (lessons learned):
- For regulated customers, SSO + firewall testing added ~7 business days — account for this in plan.
- Early prefix caching reduced token cost by 18% for a search workload; capture caching config as part of the runbook.
- Always capture a functional baseline video during go-live (valuable for troubleshooting).

Quick links (internal artifacts):
- SE integration checklist: /internal/se/runbooks/integration-checklist
- Billing anomalies playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Finance/Billing-Anomalies
- Evals + quality regression alert docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Evals

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we mandate a 30-day exec touch for all >$50k ARR deals? (Discussion for GTM/CS leadership)
- Do we require an on-prem checklist variant for Private deployments? (note: take to product-private-deployments)

Revision history:
- 2024-11-05 — Draft created (Ava Martinez)
- 2024-11-12 — Added rescue play and sample emails (Jun Park)

End of doc.
